Three offices make up the Tax Department: Assessing, Collections and Land Records. They share the Hardison Building at 117 Beasley Street, Kenansville, and keep weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

Duplin County tax offices
OfficeWhat it doesPhone
AssessingSets values on real and personal property and takes exclusion and present-use applications910-296-2110
CollectionsCollects county and town taxes, runs delinquent collection and foreclosures, issues mobile home moving permits910-296-2112
Land RecordsMaintains parcel maps and who owns what910-296-2110 (general tax questions)

Mail goes to Box 968, Kenansville, NC 28349. Collections handles town levies along with county bills for Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace and Warsaw. Walk in with cash, a check or a card, call, or use the online portal. Cards cost extra every time.

sections.h2: The housing market for a seller
sections.html:
Rural Duplin had about 51,571 residents in July 2025, after falling from 58,505 (2010) to 48,715 (2020). Of its 24,235 housing units, 70.3% are owner-occupied, with a median value of $137,400. Median gross rent is $865 and median household income is $55,148.

Ahead of listing, get a payoff figure from the collector and learn from the assessor whether an exclusion is on file.

The county's recommended budget for 2026-27 keeps the rate at 58 cents for every $100 of assessed value. That matches the year before, which was a 15.5-cent cut from the 73.5 cents budgeted for 2024-25 after the January 2025 revaluation.

  • Revaluation in 2025 lifted the tax base by about 25% and brought assessments to roughly 98 percent of market value.
  • The revenue-neutral rate it produced was $0.5667 per $100.
  • Billed value for 2026 is $6,143,053,057 of real and personal property, spread over 42,374 nonexempt parcels as of January 2026.
  • Fire districts add their own rate to the county's. The 2025-26 recommended budget runs from 4.5 cents per $100 (Calypso department) up to 10 cents (Harrells department).

The fire district and town for a parcel decide its full rate, and the assessing office can tell you both. With values near market, a buyer's lender will see a tax load that matches the real price.

Current values date from a January 1, 2025 revaluation. The next is planned for January 1, 2030. The state minimum is every eight years, yet commissioners chose in 2023 to reappraise countywide every five.

Between cycles, assessing staff go through building permits for new construction and additions and talk with owners about value. The next reappraisal will be carried out by state-certified appraisers. Anything you built, added or tore down since the last one has probably already reached the appraisers by way of the permit.

Begin with the county's informal review form. It asks for the owner, appellant, parcel number, address and your opinion of value. You circle the basis of the appeal: appraisal, asking price, purchase price or comparable sales.

  • Attach photos or documents that back up your number. Missing evidence can delay the review.
  • Commercial or income property owners include their three latest years of income and expenses.
  • Mail the form to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville, NC 28349. The current form lists April 15 as the submission date.
  • A separate form handles personal property appeals and requests a Board of Equalization and Review hearing.

State law has the county board meet for the first time between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May. If the ruling goes against you, send the Property Tax Commission written notice of your grounds within 30 days of the mailing date, and copy the assessor.

September 1 is the due date, and anything paid before January 6 is free of interest. After that, 2% applies through the start of February, and 3/4% is added for each later month or fraction of a month.

The collector can use:

  • Wage garnishment.
  • Seizure of grower payments.
  • Bank account attachment.
  • State income tax refund attachment.
  • Foreclosure on the property.

A tax foreclosure runs like a mortgage foreclosure. The county attorney receives the delinquent file, the court picks a sale date, and a sign goes up on the property while notices run in local papers. Bidding takes place at the Kenansville courthouse steps and starts at the county's bid. Whoever bids highest puts down 20% that day in cash or certified check. Once the commissioner files the sale report, anyone has 10 days to raise the bid or file exceptions. Until confirmation, the owner may redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Assessing processes the senior, disability and disabled veteran exclusions plus present-use value applications for farmland. Its forms include an application for property tax relief, a certification of disability and a certification for the disabled veteran exclusion.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the larger of $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, for owners 65 and up or totally and permanently disabled whose income is under the cap ($38,800 for tax year 2026).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the home's appraised value, at any age and income.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4% of income (5% for incomes between the cap and 150% of it), and anything above is deferred.

File with the county assessor, who must take applications until June 1 before the tax year. If you own a mobile home, note that no moving permit comes from the collector until the taxes are paid or shown not to be at risk.

Request a payoff from collections, find out which fire district and town taxes apply, and let your attorney settle the year's tax at closing. The seller also buys the deed stamp, a different charge, at the register of deeds.

If you inherited a house with back taxes, ask whether Collections has already sent it to the county attorney, because that shortens your time. A cash buyer may close before a sale date is set, and cash skips the lender's appraisal and approval steps. In both cases the payoff is paid from the proceeds. Call Collections at 910-296-2112 for the number.

On sale day, expect to bring the latest bill, any exclusion approvals and a list of every open year. The closing attorney then asks Collections for a final payoff that includes the town levy if the parcel is inside Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw. Paying the whole balance at closing keeps the buyer's title free of tax claims and avoids a delay when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When is the next Duplin County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2030. The latest took effect January 1, 2025, and commissioners voted in 2023 to revalue every five years.

faqs.q: How do I pay Duplin County property tax?
faqs.a: Go to the Tax Office at 117 Beasley Street in Kenansville, call 910-296-2112, or use the online tax portal. In person you can use cash, check or card, and cards carry a fee.

faqs.q: What rate does Duplin County charge?
faqs.a: The recommended 2026-27 budget uses 58 cents per $100 of assessed value. Fire districts and towns collected by the county add more, so ask the assessing office for your parcel's full rate.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Duplin County assessment?
faqs.a: Mail the informal real property review form with evidence to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville. It lists April 15 as the submission date, and commercial owners add three years of income and expense figures.

faqs.q: What happens if Duplin County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: The county can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, grower payments and state refunds, or foreclose. Foreclosure sales are on the courthouse steps in Kenansville, with a 20% deposit from the winning bidder.
